messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate (502/504) + latency spike observed in smart-routing decision plane for multi-region requests. Region: eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Auto-fallbacks increasing. Paging on-call.

sam_oncall: I'm up — looking now. Seeing 5xx spike starting ~1752345600. Smart-routing service showing lots of region fallback requests and model-variant mismatches.

nora_sre: I can see increased connections to the 'quant-v2-small' pool from eu clients that should be hitting 'prod-base-v1'. Some health checks for quant-v2-small are flaky. Could be DNS or routing map mismatch.

sam_oncall: Can someone post a quick dig from an edge node? I want to confirm which endpoint the edge is resolving.

kaushal: Ran dig from a vulnerable edge POP:

```
$ dig +short smart.redwood.api.eu-west-1
10.10.200.4
10.10.20.4
```

But the control-plane mapping for eu-west-1 currently points at 10.10.20.99 (prod-base pool). Those IPs above are from an old canary pool that was retired yesterday.

jen_prodeng: That smells like stale DNS cache at the edge (TTL winddown not complete) + smart-routing fallback policy aggressively moving traffic when it sees errors -> fallback to retired pool -> more errors -> more fallback.

ops-bot: Action items: 1) Disable automatic fallback policy for smart-routing (temporary). 2) Bypass edge cache by setting override header to force fresh resolution. 3) Notify customers with impacted requests.

sam_oncall: I'm disabling auto-fallback now.

sam_oncall: `./rctl routing set --service smart-routing --auto-fallback=false --who sam_oncall` -> returned OK.

nora_sre: Good. Next, can we force DNS TTL refresh at the major CDNs? Fastly and Cloudflare show cached A records for the retired pool.

kaushal: Submitting purge to Fastly for smart.redwood.api.* and triggering Cloudflare zone purge. fastly-bot will confirm.

fastly-bot: Fastly purge submitted: purge id fd12e3. Cache TTLs invalidated for matching hosts. Propagation ~30s-2m.

support-esk: Customer ops: we have multiple support tickets reporting intermittent 502s and long tail latencies. Logged affected customer orgs: AcmeGames, NimbusPay (EU). Estimating ~0.8% of production requests in last 12m.

product-ops: Preparing a short incident banner and a targeted email for enterprise customers in EU. ETA 10m.

kaushal: Also checked Route53: record for smart.redwood.api.eu-west-1 was updated to the new vip list (10.10.20.*) at 1752345400 with TTL=300. Some edge POPs still resolving the older VIPs due to CDN caches.

sam_oncall: Any evidence of config drift in the routing policy? Maybe an older rollout got re-applied.

nora_sre: I checked the gitops history — no recent rollbacks. However the rollout orchestrator retried a failed canary job last night and re-applied a mapping to the retired canary pool under a different tag. It looks like the orchestrator used a stale manifest from the artifact registry.

jen_prodeng: So two contributing factors: 1) Stale CDN caching of A records + TTL, 2) Orchestrator re-applied stale routing manifest that points to retired pool. Automatic fallback amplified the loop.

sam_oncall: Mitigations applied: 1) Auto-fallback disabled (done). 2) Fastly/CF cache purge (done). 3) Reverted orchestrator application to the correct manifest (rolling back the stale mapping) — `kubectl apply -f manifests/smart-routing/prod-v2.yml@sha:abc123`.

ops-bot: Note: rolling back mapping triggered a small config reload on 6 edge gateways; those reloads were gradual and did not report errors.

kaushal: I'm verifying traffic now. Metrics starting to normalise. 5xx rate dropping from 3.1% to 0.4% over last 2 mins.

support-esk: P1 tickets: updated customers, ETA for full resolution: 20 min. Logged temporary credit for impacted customers, pending AMA.

product-ops: Live banner posted on status page: "Partial routing disruption affecting EU requests; mitigation in progress." Link: https://status.redwood.internal/incident/1752345678

nora_sre: Quick postmortem note: TTLs were left at 300 after canary retire; follow-up action to reduce TTL before canary rotation window and ensure CDN purge post-rotation.

sam_oncall: Handing off to night oncall (jen_prodeng) in 30m for monitoring and post-incident cleanup. Creating an incident ticket with timeline.

jen_prodeng: Taking handoff at 1752345900. I'll keep an eye for any regression and start an incident doc (link to internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/create/1752345678).

support-esk: Final customer impact summary for handoff: ~0.8% of requests affected, primary impact EU dedicated customers, degraded RT and 502s for ~25 minutes. No data loss.

sam_oncall: Adding immediate action items for postmortem: 1) Add an orchestrator artifact validation check before apply. 2) Change canary retire playbook to auto-purge CDN and lower TTL for 1 hour. 3) Make fallback throttling (instead of binary) so it doesn't oscillate.

jen_prodeng: Acknowledged. Will open RFC and assign owners. Also scheduling a meeting with CDN contacts to understand long-lived caches on some POPs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Error rates returned to baseline. Auto-fallback remains disabled until postmortem complete. Incident duration ~32m.

sam_oncall: Thx team. Leaving notes and logs in the incident ticket. If anything spikes again, re-open thread.
